Orthokeratology (OrthoK) lenses are specially designed contact lenses worn overnight. They gently reshape the cornea while sleeping, allowing clear vision during the day without glasses or contact lenses.
We find that families find this particularly useful when their children are playing sports. There are families that prefer their kids to not wear glasses and they find this useful too.
In children, OrthoK lenses are also used as part of myopia management to help slow progression in selected cases. Proper evaluation, precise fitting, and regular follow-up are essential to ensure safety and effectiveness.

Doctors recommend OrthoK after assessing eye measurements, corneal health, and suitability for the child’s age and lifestyle.

Book an appointment to evaluate OrthoK suitability.

Myopia (short-sightedness) often begins in childhood and may increase as a child grows. Lately, we have been seeing this growth continue upto even 18-19 years of age which is a concern. The Myopia Control Clinic at Eye Solutions focuses on early assessment, monitoring progression, and offering evidence-based strategies to help manage myopia.

Each child undergoes a detailed vision and eye health evaluation, followed by personalised guidance based on age, eye measurements, and lifestyle factors. Management plans are designed to support long-term visual health while fitting into a child’s daily routine.

Early evaluation allows parents to understand progression patterns and available options clearly.

Book an appointment at the Myopia Control Clinic.

Squint occurs when the eyes do not align properly, causing each eye to focus in a different direction. In children, this can interfere with normal visual development and may lead to reduced vision in one eye if not monitored early. Some children may not complain of vision problems, making regular eye checks important.

In adults, squint can cause eye strain, headaches, double vision, or difficulty with depth perception. It may develop gradually or appear suddenly due to changes in vision, nerve function, or muscle balance.

Squint is not always constant and may appear only during fatigue, illness, or prolonged screen use. Early assessment helps identify whether the squint is intermittent or persistent and whether it affects visual function.

An eye examination allows doctors to evaluate eye alignment, vision, and binocular function and advise on observation, correction, or treatment when needed.

Book an eye check-up for squint assessment.

Squint (misalignment of the eyes) can affect vision, depth perception, and eye comfort in both children and adults. At Eye Solutions, squint management begins with a detailed evaluation to understand the type, cause, and impact on vision.

Treatment may involve glasses, exercises, or surgical correction, depending on individual findings. Squint surgery aims to improve eye alignment and visual coordination through a planned and measured approach.

Early evaluation helps determine the most appropriate course of care and timing of treatment.

Book an appointment for a squint evaluation.

Cataracts develop slowly and often go unnoticed in the early stages. Many people assume their changing vision is simply a part of ageing, but recognising early signs can help with timely evaluation and planning.

Common early symptoms include blurred or hazy vision, increased glare from lights, difficulty driving at night, faded colours, and frequent changes in spectacle power. Some people also notice that reading becomes harder even with updated glasses.

Cataracts are not an emergency condition, but regular eye check-ups are important to monitor progression. Early assessment allows your doctor to explain the condition, discuss lifestyle impact, and advise on the right time for treatment - if and when needed.

If you are experiencing persistent visual changes or feel your vision is not as sharp as before, an eye examination can help clarify the cause and guide you appropriately.

Book an eye check-up to understand your vision better

A comprehensive eye examination checks more than just vision. It includes vision and eye power assessment, cataract evaluation, eye pressure measurement, and screening for diabetic eye disease.

Using a wide-angle fundus camera, we can capture nearly 90% of the retina in a single image - often without dilating eye drops. This avoids the waiting time and temporary blurred vision that dilation can cause.

Eye pressure checks help detect changes that, if uncontrolled, may lead to a condition called glaucoma. These tests help doctors assess overall eye health and guide further care when needed.

Book an appointment for a comprehensive eye check-up.

Cataracts cause gradual clouding of the natural lens, leading to blurred vision, glare, and difficulty with daily activities. At Eye Solutions, cataract surgery is planned carefully after a detailed evaluation of your eye health and visual needs.

The procedure involves replacing the cloudy lens with a clear artificial lens to improve vision clarity. Our focus is on safe techniques, precise measurements, and a calm, patient-centric approach - from consultation to recovery.

If you or a family member are experiencing vision changes, an eye examination can help determine the next step.

Call now to schedule an evaluation.

Signs Your Child Needs an Eye Checkup in Mumbai 

Children rarely complain about their vision.

Not because nothing is wrong, but because they have no reference point for what clear vision should feel like. If a child has always seen the world in a certain way, they may simply assume that is how everyone sees it.

This is why parents and caregivers play such an important role in spotting the early signs that a child may need an eye examination.

Signs worth paying attention to include:
1. Squinting when looking at distant objects or a screen
2. Sitting unusually close to the television or holding books very near the face
3. Complaints of headaches, particularly after reading or schoolwork
4. Rubbing the eyes frequently
5. Tilting the head to one side when focusing
6. A noticeable drop in concentration or academic performance

None of these signs individually confirm a vision problem, but one or more of them together suggest that a thorough eye examination is worthwhile.

From age 4 years onwards, a routine annual eye examination for kids is recommended even if no symptoms present. 

At Phiroze M. Dastoor & Co., Pedder Road, our specialist team conducts comprehensive eye examinations for children, tailored to their age and developmental stage.

Early attention supports healthy visual development.

Struggling with Colour Vision? Visit Phiroze M. Dastoor & Co. 

Colour vision deficiency is often discovered by chance.

A comment from a family member. A test at school. A moment of uncertainty when trying to distinguish between two colours that others seem to differentiate with ease.

For many people, it has simply always been this way, and they have never sought a formal assessment or explored what options might be available to them.

A structured colour vision assessment provides clarity. It identifies the specific type of colour vision deficiency present, its severity, and whether any supportive options such as specialist lenses may be of benefit.

Understanding your colour vision is also relevant in certain professional contexts, as some careers and licensing requirements involve colour vision standards. A formal assessment provides documented results that can be used for these purposes.

At Phiroze M. Dastoor & Co., Pedder Road, our specialist team conducts detailed colour vision evaluations in a calm, unhurried clinical environment.

If you or someone in your family has concerns about colour vision, a formal assessment is the most informed place to begin.

Toric Contact Lenses for Astigmatism – Available at Phiroze M. Dastoor & Co.

If you have astigmatism and have tried standard contact lenses before, you may have found that they do not provide the clarity you were hoping for.

Astigmatism occurs when the cornea or natural lens of the eye has an irregular curvature, causing light to focus at more than one point on the retina. Standard spherical contact lenses are not designed to correct this, so vision can remain blurred or distorted even when wearing them.

Toric contact lenses are specifically designed for eyes with astigmatism. These lenses have different powers in different meridians of the lens and are generally weighted to remain correctly oriented on the eye.

Other materials are available for more irregular or higher cylindrical corrections, with bespoke fits helping achieve maximum comfort and vision.

When fitted accurately, toric lenses can provide clear, stable vision throughout the day for patients with astigmatism who prefer contact lenses over spectacles.

The right fit depends on a precise contact lens assessment, fit and follow up.

At Phiroze M. Dastoor & Co., Pedder Road, our team conducts thorough assessments to ensure the most appropriate lens is recommended for your individual prescription and ocular health.

Early Cataract Signs – Advice from Phiroze M. Dastoor & Co. 

Cataracts develop slowly, and that is precisely what makes them easier to miss in the early stages.

The natural lens inside the eye gradually becomes cloudy over time, affecting how much light and how well it passes through to the retina. In the early stages, colours may appear slightly less vivid. Vision may seem a little hazy, particularly in bright light or at night. Contrast sensitivity may change noticeably for people with certain visual demands.

Common early signs include:
1. Increased sensitivity to glare, especially when driving at night
2. Colours appearing less bright or slightly yellowed
3. A gradual blurring of vision that does not improve with a new glasses prescription
4. Difficulty reading in low light conditions

These changes often develop so gradually that they are attributed to ageing rather than a specific condition. This is why regular specialist eye examinations are important, particularly from middle age onwards.

Are vision correction treatments like LASIK Safe? 

It is one of the most common questions we hear.

LASIK is a laser-based vision correction procedure that reshapes the cornea, the clear, front surface of the eye, to reduce or eliminate the need for glasses or contact lenses. It has been performed for decades and has an excellent, established safety profile.

The honest answer to whether procedures like LASIK are safe is: for the right patient, yes. But determining who the right patient is requires time, detailed investigation and precision technology.

Not everyone is a suitable candidate. The health and thickness of the cornea, the overall structure of the eye, and the stability of the visual system are all factors that must be carefully evaluated before a recommendation is made.
